Win prizes RPG Hub Jump To: Quick links Top deals Live updates Hardware I'm building the ultimate GTA 6 setup this Prime Day, these are the gadgets in my cart Your guide to GTA 6-ready upgrades News By Duncan Robertson Last updated 6 October 2026 0 Comments Join the conversation When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here's how it works . Jump To: Quick links Top deals Live updates Menu (Image credit: Future) 1. Quick links 2. The setup 3. Live updates GTA 6 is nearly upon us, and with just a few weeks left to build that ultimate setup Amazon's Prime Day couldn't have come at a better time. We've been waiting so patiently, for so long, it seems right to herald in this new era of GTA with something a little special. Whether you're wondering which TV will let that Xbox sparkle or finally giving in to the allure of the pro controller, there's plenty of kit out there designed to make your time in GTA 6 all the more satisfying. Thankfully, the Prime Big Deals event is currently underway and I've been scouring the shelves for all the discounts that will make that first boot feel even more warm and fuzzy. From the best gaming TVs to the best sound systems, these are the Prime Day PS5 deals and Xbox savings I'd use to kit out the ultimate GTA 6 setup. We're not just grabbing any old tat here, though. Oh no, these are discounts on the tech we've been hands on with and recommend every day. You'll find our absolute top picks just below, our favorite TV, controller, headset, and sound system also taking part in this week's Prime Day offers. Of course, we're still roaming those virtual aisles and you'll find all our latest picks further down the page. Quick links TVs: from $207 at Amazon Controllers: from $21 at Amazon Headsets: from $29 at Amazon Monitors: from $122 at Amazon Soundbars: from $99 at Amazon The setup so far The TV Save $94.26 Hisense U7 55-inch: was $694.25 now $599.99 at Amazon Hisense TVs usually take the top spots of our budget round-ups, and while our absolute favorite model isn't discounted, this more advanced mini LED set is. A 14% discount brings it to just $10 off its lowest-ever price. Larger models are discounted too: the 65-inch and 75-inch versions are both half price, to their lowest-ever costs, though still cost more than the 55-inch version. Hisense U7 review View Deal The controller Save $33 Scuf Omega: was $219.99 now $186.99 at Amazon If you're running on PS5, the Scuf Omega is going to be the Prime Day controller deal to beat ahead of GTA 6. It's taken its first ever discount and, while it's still pretty hefty, you're looking at a lower price compared to the Victrix Pro BFG and DualSense Edge here. Scuf Omega review View Deal The headset Save $40 SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni: was $399.99 now $359.99 at Amazon Our absolute favorite gaming headset isn't cheap, even with this discount which brings it to its lowest-ever price. But it's the ultimate in personal gaming audio, so if your budget can reach, it's well worth picking up. Just note, only the blue option is reduced. SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni View Deal The sound system Save $149.20 Q Acoustics M20 HD: was $878.20 now $729 at Amazon Our overall favorite sound system for gaming is the Q Acoustics M20 HD, which works just as well for either console (as it does for your TV or PC). It's enjoying a rare discount down to what seems to be its lowest price so far, so grab that $150 saving while you can. Q Acoustics M20 HD review View Deal Live updates Get notified of updates 2026-10-06T19:23:46.296Z I think this is the perfect mid-budget monitor to play GTA 6 on, but I'm biased (Image credit: LG) I have a slightly older version of this gaming monitor, but I can tell you I paid quite a bit more for it than $159.99, which is where it's priced for Prime Day. Personally, I'll be playing GTA 6 on my 65" 4K TV, but if you have your PS5 or Xbox plugged into a PC monitor and you want to upgrade your kit before November 19, I would recommend this one if it's within your target budget. I've been gaming on an LG screen very similar to this one for a few years now, and it has yet to let me down. The 1440p screen, which I think is the sweet spot for performance and image quality on a budget, looks fantastic and the 200Hz refresh rate ensures a consistently smooth image in motion. I also like how intuitive the on-screen settings menu is, which allows you to toggle on and off a huge variety of features for the price. For my money, it's tough to beat this screen in the sub-$200 field, especially with this Prime Day deal. LG 27G61ZB-B 27-inch Ultragear gaming monitor | $159.99 at Amazon 2026-10-06T17:59:02.211Z Prep your ears for GTA 6 with my trusty Sony INZONE H3 wired headset for just $68 (Image credit: Sony) Tabitha spotlighted a $60 headset from SteelSeries earlier today as an alternative to the $300 gaming headsets you see all over the place, and I'd like to highlight another option from Sony in preparation for GTA 6. I've been using the Sony INZONE H3 wired headset for almost three years now, and it has yet to let me down. I paid the full $120 retail price when I bought it, and I don't regret the purchase one bit. Sound quality is great, spatial audio is immersive, and build quality seems solid. If you want to immerse yourself in GTA 6 without any distractions and don't want to spend hundreds of dollars when everything is already exorbitantly expensive as it is, I can't recommend this first-party Sony headset enough - and since it's wired for 3mm jacks, you should have no compatibility issues using it on Xbox if that's your preferred platform. Sony INZONE H3 wired headset | $68 on Amazon 2026-10-06T16:21:51.313Z If you're looking for the DualSense Edge, you're out of luck (Image credit: Future / Duncan Robertson) I can totally appreciate that if you want a bit more controller for your money on PS5, you want the official PS5 pro controller, especially since it's the only one on the platform that will give you haptic feedback. Annoyingly, Sony is playing hardball and across all of the retailers, there are no DualSense Edge discounts. Sorry about that, but rest assured I'll be checking as Prime Day continues on over the next few days. 2026-10-06T16:03:57.497Z Looking for new speakers? (Image credit: Future / Duncan Robertson) These aren't on sale, but if you're looking for a more affordable sound system ahead of GTA 6's launch, I can recommend the Logitech Z407 2.1 setup. These are our favorite computer speakers, and while they aren't discounted, they hold a whole lot of value for gamers connecting up to different platforms. These are ones I use every day, so I can vouch for them, especially if you want good sound quality on a budget. Logitech Z407 speakers: $115 at Amazon 2026-10-06T15:54:18.543Z Oh, and um, here's the game (Image credit: Rockstar) Maybe I should have said before now but no GTA 6 setup is complete without the actual game itself, so if you're yet to pre-order, here's Amazon selling you a code in the box if you don't want to buy directly from Sony or Microsoft. GTA 6 pre-order: $79.99 at Amazon 2026-10-06T15:39:06.314Z To OLED or not to OLED, that is the question (Image credit: Rockstar) A game that looks as good as this one might be motivating you to look for a new gaming display, and personally, I don't think TVs and monitors get any better than OLEDs. There's only one problem: OLEDs are expensive, and with extremely high refresh rates that surpass what the PS5 and Xbox can do, maybe they're overkill for GTA 6 unless you're waiting for the PC release. If you are looking to go OLED on GTA 6, I don't blame you, but here's my buying advice as someone who shopped around and saved up for one for years before I managed to get one. Don't automatically go for the most up-to-date model. Especially on the LG side of things, annual updates are incremental at best, so if you're still able to get one from a few generations ago at a more reasonable price, you probably aren't going to miss out on much. For example, the LG OLED C4, which I have, is a stunningly good TV with a 144Hz refresh rate - more than enough for me to harness it for high frame rate PC gaming. It's somehow still available at Amazon despite the current gen being the C6. I'd recommend the 55-inch model, which is available for $1,195 - that's about $200 more than I paid for it about a year and a half ago, but it's a good price for this size. Alternatively, if you want the C6 but you're not massively fussed about the size, go for the 42-inch model, which is somehow cheaper at $999. LG OLED C4 55-inch: $1,195 at Amazon LG OLED C6 42-inch: $999.99 at Amazon If neither of these float your boat, there are also loads of OLED monitors out there? 2026-10-06T15:30:09.730Z I was going to ask if you wanted to play GTA 6 in VR, but nevermind (Image credit: Future / Duncan Robertson) I had this whole post planned where I was going to tell you that if you harnessed the power of PSVR 2's cinematic mode, you could play GTA 6 in VR - which would also be a perfect solution for when your family members, partner, or flatmates needed to use the TV and you didn't want to stop playing the game. Annoyingly, PSVR 2 seems to be so low on stock that you can hardly buy it anywhere, and if you can, it's way, way above price and will probably be a pre-owned version anyway. I even checked PlayStation's Direct retailer and in the US, the headset isn't even listed as far as I can see. I'll keep checking for stock because I do think it'd be amazing to play this game in VR with tiny OLED displays booting it into your eyeballs, but I don't recommend buying the headset at higher than its $399 price. 2026-10-06T15:18:20.080Z PS5 players, I see you (Image credit: Future / Duncan Robertson) There are loads of pro controller options for Xbox gamers, but surprisingly few for PS5 - especially when it comes to ones that don't break the bank. The Razer Wolverine V2 Pro is a bit older now - so much so that Razer has literally just announced the V4 Pro for Xbox - but that means it's one of the most deal-prone PS5 pro controllers you can find. It's currently seeing a discount down from its $215 original price (which, to be fair, we never see it at these days) down to $134. Razer Wolverine V2 Pro: $134.99 at Amazon 2026-10-06T15:03:39.361Z The hunt for PS5 SSDs isn't going so well (Image credit: Future / Duncan Robertson) As I mentioned before, the PS5 SSD market is in flames. If I were you, I'd look at any of these at Amazon that you feel are appealing to your budget if you really need the extra storage space. If it's not an absolute must for you though, I'd avoid buying one at all right now - seriously, the prices are just that bad. If I had to pick a favorite, it'd be this Acer Predator GM7 1TB drive, which is going for $159.99 in a Prime Day deal. Just remember that you'll need a heatsink for it because these types of drives generate a lot of heat and if you don't keep them cool, you'll do damage to it and the internals of your console. I've linked to my favorite heatsink below too. Thankfully, that's actually at a genuinely low cost. Acer Predator GM7 1TB: $159.99 at Amazon Sabrent PS5 SSD Heatsink: $11.89 at Amazon 2026-10-06T14:48:03.132Z On a similar note, here's a more budget-friendly controller for Xbox players (Image credit: Future / Duncan Robertson) Again, this will be one for Xbox players first and foremost, but if you're looking for an Xbox controller that's a bit more friendly on your wallet, the GameSir G7 Pro is definitely, definitely worth looking at. This is one of the best value gamepads on the shelves currently, and it'd be the perfect companion for exploring Vice City. GameSir G7 Pro: $79.99 $63.99 at Amazon 2026-10-06T14:29:26.418Z While I look for storage, here's an excellent mid-range headset for you (Image credit: Future / Duncan Robertson) Let's say you don't have the money to afford the pricey, top-of-the-line SteelSeries headset I mentioned above, but you want something a bit more premium than the budget option. I'd turn to the Fractal Scape, a gaming headset with a very comfortable, high-end, and feature-rich feel to it. It's seeing a $30 saving at a bunch of retailers at the moment, and since it's one I use almost daily, it's a headset I very much recommend. Fractal Scape: $199.99 $169.99 at Amazon 2026-10-06T14:13:27.906Z It's a horrible time to go looking for extra storage but I'll do my best (Image credit: Future / Duncan Robertson) I wouldn't blame you if storage space was a worry with GTA 6 coming up. It's amazing how one big game can start to eat up the little console storage we have as standard, and even if GTA 6 is the only game you might care about for a while, it's still good to have a bit of spare. Unfortunately, you couldn't think of a worse time to shop for a spare PS5 SSD because AI companies are stealing all of the world's supply and consumer prices have skyrocketed. That said, bear with me, I'm going to see what bargains I can find on some internal or external SSDs this Prime Day. 2026-10-06T14:06:51.663Z The controller I'd recommend for Xbox players (Image credit: Future / Duncan Robertson) If you're going to be playing GTA 6 on an Xbox console, I'd shoot for the Nacon Revolution X Unlimited as your controller pick. It's probably my favorite feature-rich, premium Xbox controller, and with its current price being down to $149.99 at Best Buy in its Xbox 360 Anniversary colorway, it's an absolute bargain. If you're sticking with Amazon for Prime Day, you can grab the original black colorway in a Big Deal Days discount, but it's not quite as low as Best Buy's. Nacon Revolution X Unlimited Anniversary Edition: $199.99 $149.99 at Best Buy Nacon Revolution X Unlimited: $199.99 $169.99 at Amazon 2026-10-06T13:50:38.636Z Don't want to spend $300+ on a headset for GTA 6? (Image credit: Future/Rosalie Newcombe) Allow me to introduce the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni's cheaper sibling. The Nova 3P sits at the bottom of SteelSeries' price ladder, and doesn't feature the hot-swappable batteries, easy multi-platform switching, or the top-grade Hi-Res audio of the Omni. It does, however, cost you a mere $59.99 this Prime Day. The wireless headset has dropped back to its record-low price at Woot this week, a fantastic rate I've only seen a handful of times this year so far. It's not going to be an upgrade if you already have an older headset that might have cost you between $100 and $200, but if you're currently relying on TV speakers and want something a little closer it will do the job particularly well for its price. SteelSeries Arctis Nova 3P | $109.99 $59.99 at Woot 2026-10-06T13:36:21.015Z One way to save on a GTA 6 Ultimate Edition pre-order (Image credit: Rockstar) It's pretty difficult to shave cash off that GTA 6 pre-order these days, this is the biggest release
